criteria.note: The intent behind 'gluten free tteok' — is tteok safe? — is answered directly in the opening two paragraphs, including the crucial 밀떡 exception, well inside 200 words.

Title is 38 chars + 20-char appended suffix = 58, description is ~147 chars, keyword 'Gluten-Free Tteok' present in the title, and the description carries new information rather than restating the title.
Headings carry the argument rather than label sections — a skimmer moves from 'glutinous is not gluten' to '밀떡 is wheat' to price to home-making without reading the body.
Four distinct internal destinations (hidden-gluten guide, celiac travel guide, Monil2 House place page) each placed where the reader would actually want them.
All three FAQ answers — the 밀떡 caveat, the Gluten Intolerance Group sourcing, and the celiac-vs-ingredients distinction — are established in the body and each stands alone as a rich result.

Concrete on price and purchase (6,000 won for three, 500 won for condensed milk) and on shared bakery counters, but the home-cooking core is deliberately non-specific and no cafe, date, or batch detail anchors it.
criteria.evidence_quote: I'm not going to hand you exact gram-by-gram ratios, because I worked mostly by feel and I'd rather not invent precision I didn't measure.

criteria.note: Korean terms are given with hangul and romanisation throughout (찹쌀가루 chapssal-garu, 밀떡 mil-tteok, 타피오카 전분 tapioka jeonbun), plus the exact regulation number and the label strings a reader can search for on a bag.
Both load-bearing claims are linked to primary sources, and the Korean labelling standard carries an explicit notice number and publication date.

The piece states plainly what it cannot establish — no category survey, no proof from absence of symptoms, no standing clearance — and publicly withdraws an unverifiable product claim; Coupang is named as plain text with no commercial link.

findings.quote: So I did. I ordered **glutinous rice flour and tapioca starch**, picked up a **mold**, and gave it a go.
findings.why: The home-making section — the article's headline claim that this is cheaper and easy — is the thinnest part on first-hand detail: no brand of flour bought, no vendor, no mold size, no month, no ratio, and nothing that went wrong. Readers and Google both read that section as generic advice rather than lived reporting.
findings.fix: Add two or three checkable observations from the actual batch: where the flours were bought and roughly what the 1kg bags cost, the mold type/size, approximate volumes used, and one thing that misfired (too dense, too sticky to unmold, steaming time). It does not require inventing gram precision — 'roughly two parts rice flour to one part starch, and my first batch was too soft to unmold' is honest and specific.

findings.quote: That whole pile is covered in our [hidden-gluten guide](/blog/hidden-gluten-korean-food).
findings.why: The same hidden-gluten URL is linked three times in the body plus once in the Related guides list. Repeated anchors to one destination dilute the value of each and leave other clearly relevant pages (place listings, snack guides) unlinked.
findings.fix: Keep one in-body link to the hidden-gluten guide at the tteokbokki paragraph, drop one of the two later repeats, and use the freed anchor for a different relevant page — e.g. a packaged-snack or label-reading guide at the '읽어야 할 원재료명' point.

findings.quote: <!-- IMG: 01.webp — homemade butter tteok, first batch, top-down on a plate. Caption: "Our first home batch — not bad at all." -->
findings.why: The only image on a dessert-recipe-adjacent post is left as an HTML comment, so nothing renders. A post about a visual food trend ships with zero images, alt text, or Image-object signal — a real loss for a query type where image results and visual snippets drive clicks.
findings.fix: Insert the actual image with descriptive alt text ('homemade butter tteok, first batch, glutinous rice flour and tapioca starch') and the caption already written, or remove the placeholder comment so it does not read as unfinished.

findings.why: 'Butter tteok' appears in both the title and the description, and the title's colon structure repeats 'Tteok' twice in 38 characters, which wastes SERP real estate on a query where the differentiator is the 밀떡 warning.
findings.fix: Consider a title that spends the second half on the differentiator rather than repeating the noun, e.g. 'Gluten-Free Tteok: Which Kinds Are Safe' or 'Is Tteok Gluten-Free? Butter Tteok (2026)', keeping under the 60-char budget with the appended site suffix.

findings.quote: since the sauce is gochujang (usually wheat) and the fish cake mixed in is typically bound with wheat starch
findings.why: Flagging for the accuracy judge only, not scored here: 'usually wheat' for gochujang and 'typically bound with wheat starch' for fish cake are unsourced frequency claims sitting next to otherwise carefully sourced statements, which is a consistency gap in an article that elsewhere cites a notice number.
findings.fix: Either attach the same standard of sourcing used for the labelling notice (a named product's 원재료명, or a link) or soften to 'commonly contains wheat — check the label', consistent with the article's own rule.

criteria.note: Safety-critical claims are sourced (GIG, MFDS 고시) or marked as observation, but a cluster of retail and recipe claims is asserted flatly with neither citation nor first-person framing — none of them affects a safety decision.
criteria.evidence_quote: they turn up in the baking aisle of the larger supermarkets, in the baking-supply shops (만월상회 and similar), and on Coupang and the usual online malls

criteria.note: Product names, the price observation, the GIG URL, and the 고시 제2025-60호 citation with its MFDS link are all checkable and internally consistent, and an unverifiable product claim was withdrawn rather than retained.

The piece states how it knows each thing — a cited FAQ, a read of the notice text, its own purchases, its own kitchen — and names what that cannot establish, including the un-surveyed cafe category and the deliberately unmeasured ratios.

No absolute clearance is offered for any shop-bought item, cross-contamination is addressed at cafe, mill, and assembly level, and celiac risk is explicitly separated from and rated above gluten sensitivity.
The GIG retrieval, the 고시 date of 29 August 2025, and the August 2026 read are all stated, and reformulation risk is flagged as a reason the whole piece has a shelf life.

Terms, romanisations, and product categories are correct, and the mandatory-allergen scope is stated precisely — 밀 designated, 보리 and 호밀 not — along with the maker's discretion over 'unavoidable' carry-over.
The reader gets specific label strings to search for (밀, 소맥분, 같은 제조시설), two sourcing search terms, direct links to both the GIG answer and the notice text, and questions to put to a cafe.

findings.quote: they turn up in the baking aisle of the larger supermarkets, in the baking-supply shops (만월상회 and similar), and on Coupang and the usual online malls
findings.why: Retail availability and the '1kg bags are the common format' detail are stated as fact with no citation and no 'we found' framing, in a piece that sources its safety claims carefully. A reader cannot tell whether this is a shopping trip or an assumption.
findings.fix: Mark it as observation — e.g. 'as of August 2026 we found both in…' — or drop the specificity about bag sizes and named shops.

findings.quote: published Korean versions add egg, sugar and milk
findings.why: Attribution to a class of sources without naming or linking any of them. It is the only recipe-composition claim in the piece not tied to something the author personally mixed.
findings.fix: Link one or two of the published recipes, or rewrite as 'the versions we looked at added…'.

findings.why: The opening asserts flatly that the specific shop-bought butter tteok contained no gluten, which is a stronger statement than reading a recipe can support and sits in tension with the article's own later instruction to treat any shop-bought piece as unverified. It does not rise to a lapse because the correction arrives explicitly in the same piece, but the intro is the part a skimming reader keeps.
findings.fix: Narrow to the recipe rather than the purchase: 'Not in the recipe — but the rule that gets you there is narrower than "tteok is rice."'
